title: Microsoft Entra ID Governance: account discovery finds local and unassigned accounts in provisioned apps
summary: Hold: the Graph guidance incorrectly makes a signed-in user's directory role mandatory for every report read, although Microsoft also documents application access. The controls and roadmap details otherwise check out; the permissions sentence needs to distinguish delegated access from application access.

claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The general availability target is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The preview date is April CY2026.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Entra account discovery for application access governance.
claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Entra: Account Discovery for Application Access Governance."

claims.claim: Account discovery retrieves an application's users and groups, matches them to Entra identities and classifies the results.
claims.quote: Account discovery uses the Discover identities experience to retrieve users and groups from a target application, match them to corresponding users and groups in Microsoft Entra ID, and classify the results so you can bring unmanaged identities under governance.

claims.claim: Local identities have no corresponding user or group in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Local identities — Users or groups in the target application that have no corresponding user or group in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What's changing: Local identities; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Local identities can include former employees, service or shared accounts, separately provisioned users and app-created groups.
claims.quote:
These identities might belong to former employees, service accounts, users who were provisioned through a different process, groups created directly in the target application
Service accounts or shared accounts created directly in the application.

claims.claim: Unassigned identities match Entra identities but lack the app assignment required for provisioning management.
claims.quote: These identities exist in your directory but don't have the required application assignment for provisioning to manage them.

claims.claim: Assigned identities are matched, assigned and fully managed by the provisioning service.
claims.quote: Assigned identities — Users or groups that match a user or group in Microsoft Entra ID and are assigned to the enterprise application. These identities are fully managed by the provisioning service.

claims.claim: Discovery uses an application's provisioning configuration with valid credentials and a successful test connection.
claims.quote: An enterprise application configured for provisioning with valid credentials and a successful test connection.

claims.claim: Discovery requires a direct matching attribute mapping.
claims.quote: Account discovery requires a direct matching attribute for correlation.

claims.claim: Discovery uses only the first matching attribute when multiple matching attributes are configured.
claims.quote: If multiple matching attributes are configured, only the first matching attribute is used.

claims.claim: Discovery does not support expression-based transformations for matching.
claims.quote: Expression-based transformations aren't supported for matching.

claims.claim: Account discovery is enabled for all provisioning connectors except Microsoft's listed exceptions.
claims.quote: Account discovery is enabled for all provisioning connectors except those listed below.

claims.claim: Group discovery, including group memberships, is in preview.
claims.quote: Group discovery, including group memberships, is currently in preview.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Generating a discovery report takes at least 30 minutes.
claims.quote: The discovery takes at least 30 minutes to generate a report.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs
claims.claim: Microsoft's example says a report for 250,000 identities might take 12 hours or more.
claims.quote: For example, an application with 250,000 identities might take 12 hours or more to generate a discovery report.

claims.claim: Discovery results can be reviewed in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: In addition to reviewing discovered accounts in the Microsoft Entra admin center, you can use Microsoft Graph to programmatically retrieve Account discovery results.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph beta identity correlation APIs retrieve discovery reports and identities.
claims.quote:
Use the Microsoft Graph beta API to:
List identity correlation reports in the tenant.
Retrieve a specific identity correlation report.
List the identities included in a report.
Filter identities by correlation status.

claims.claim: Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise provides a preview way to investigate discovery reports.
claims.quote: You can use the Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise to investigate account discovery reports by asking questions in natural language.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1 to assign discovered users to the enterprise application or access packages.
claims.quote: After discovering users in your application, you can assign those users to the enterprise application or an access package. Download the Assign-CorrelatedUsers.ps1 file and run it in PowerShell 7.x to assign users.

claims.claim: Application administrators can create app accounts manually after provisioning onboarding.
claims.quote: After onboarding to provisioning, application administrators can manually create accounts in the application.

claims.claim: Discovery identifies access outside Entra ID Governance so it can be brought under governance.
claims.quote: Account discovery will help administrators identify access that exists outside of Microsoft Entra ID Governance and bring that access under governance

claims.claim: Provisioning attribute mappings control target attribute values and matching, not just discovery results.
claims.quote: If you enable user provisioning for a non-Microsoft SaaS application, the Microsoft Entra admin center controls its attribute values through attribute-mappings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Mismatched or outdated attribute values can prevent matching and cause identities to appear local.
claims.quote: identities that didn't match due to data quality issues (for example, mismatched or outdated attribute values).

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The target app must implement SCIM pagination under RFC 7644 section 3.4.2.4, and missing support can cause zero results.
claims.quote: If your discovery report has zero results, verify that you configured a single direct matching attribute (no expressions) in your attribute mappings. Next, verify with the application vendor that the application supports pagination in accordance with RFC 7644, Section 3.4.2.4.

claims.claim: Graph reads need ProvisioningLog.Read.All and one of the supported directory roles.
claims.quote:
| Application | ProvisioningLog.Read.All | AuditLog.Read.All |
For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role that grants the permissions required for this operation.
claims.fix: Replace the final Governance controls bullet with: 'ProvisioningLog.Read.All is the least-privileged permission for delegated and application access; AuditLog.Read.All is also accepted. For delegated work or school access, the signed-in user additionally needs a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role granting the operation's permissions.' Keep controls[1].note's least-privileged wording.
